note: Item text taken from the study's own response data file (data_cognitive_tasks/task_datasets/data_impossible_question.csv in github.com/forecastingresearch/fpt), which carries question_text on every row keyed to id. id -> question_text is strictly one-to-one: 90 distinct ids, 90 distinct (id, question_text) pairs, no id with more than one text. The IRW code IS that id -- data/data_impossible_question.py passes KWARGS {'item_col': 'id', 'resp_col': 'correct'} to fpt_common.convert_trial_based_task, which assigns df['item'] = df[item_col] -- so there is no positional or order inference (core model pattern 1). MAPPING VERIFIED BY EXACT REPRODUCTION rather than by inference: aggregating the source file's `correct` by `id` reproduces the live table's per-item row count for all 90 items and per-item mean to within 1e-12. 817 source rows carry a missing `correct` (timed-out trials) and are dropped by both the source aggregation and the IRW table. RESPONSE STRUCTURE: each trial showed three radio options -- answer_1, answer_2, and a literal 'Opt-out' -- plus a 50-100% confidence slider. correct_answer is 1, 2 or 3, where 3 marks an impossible question and 'Opt-out' is the correct response. 34 items key to answer_1, 38 to answer_2, and 18 (the IQ_* items) to Opt-out. correct_response therefore carries the text of whichever option is correct, 'Opt-out' included. option_text is left blank for every row, matching the sibling tables himmelstein-cognitive_reflection-2025 and himmelstein-number_series-2025: resp is a 0/1 correctness score, not an index over the three options, so mapping answer_1/answer_2 onto resp 0/1 would be false -- a respondent choosing answer_1 scores 1 whenever answer_1 is the key. OPT-OUT SCORING, checked against the source rather than assumed, because the instructions and the data disagree: the administered instructions say opting out means 'you won't be scored based on that answer', but in the file every GK item answered with choice 3 is scored correct=0 (3,625 rows, none scored 1), while on IQ items choice 3 is scored correct=1 (4,712 rows) and choices 1 or 2 are scored 0 (9,375 rows). So resp=1 means 'picked the keyed answer, or correctly opted out of an unanswerable question', and opting out of an answerable one is scored wrong despite what participants were told. instructions are transcribed from the jsPsych task source (materials/js/impossible_question_task.js), with the interpolated ${TEST_TRIALS_N} token replaced by the actual count of 90; the example item and the slider tick labels shown on the same instruction screen are not reproduced. The 18 IQ_* items are deliberately fabricated -- 'the battle of Kavkav', 'a Detseroid', 'Synomle' do not exist -- which is the design, not a data defect. AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED: audit_batch.R flags a row-count anomaly (median 605) and 100% blank option_text. Both are expected. The row counts are the study's anchor/AIG form design, not item-code conflation: the 30 items on the anchor form declared in the task js have n 972-1181 (median 1177) because nearly every participant saw them, while the 60 AIG-version items have n 489-607 (median 576). The split is exact -- every item with n>900 is on the anchor form and no anchor item falls below it -- and per-item n reproduces the source file exactly, so nothing was conflated. Blank option_text is the sibling convention for these 0/1-scored tables, explained above.
public_note: 18 of the 90 items (the IQ_* codes) are deliberately unanswerable: they ask about invented battles, shapes and places, and the correct response is to select 'Opt-out'. resp=1 therefore means the respondent either picked the keyed answer or correctly opted out, and resp=0 covers both a wrong answer and opting out of a question that did have an answer -- note that opting out of an answerable item is scored incorrect even though the instructions told participants it would not be scored. option_text is empty by design: each trial offered two alternatives plus 'Opt-out', but the table's resp is a 0/1 correctness score rather than which option was chosen, so the option texts cannot be mapped onto it; the correct option is given in correct_response instead.

note: ADMC Resistance to Framing (28 items, resp 1-6) and Applying Decision Rules (10 items, resp 0-3) in one table, given separate section_ids because the two subtests have different administered instructions and different response scales. Text comes from the study's own experiment source in github.com/forecastingresearch/fpt/materials/js, which keys every item to the exact identifier the data records: data/data_admc_raw.py passes item_col='admc_id', resp_col='admc_response', so the IRW code IS that id, and the js declares the same strings ('rc1_1', 'dr1', ...). No positional or order inference. Framing text is form-invariant: all four counterbalanced form files (admc_framing_a1|a2|rc1|rc2_task.js) declare the identical 28 items, and their stimulus text and endpoint labels parse byte-identical across all four, so which form file is read does not matter. CORROBORATED BY RESPONSE-RANGE FINGERPRINT: for the decision-rules items admc_response is the COUNT of correct options the participant checked (the js computes correct_answers.filter(chosen).length), so each item's number of correct answers predicts its maximum resp. Predicted maxima 1,1,1,1,1,1,1,2,3,3 for dr1-dr10 match the live data exactly, including the three items that differ from the rest (dr8 at 2, dr9 and dr10 at 3). All 28 framing items use all of 1-6. DEVIATIONS FROM LITERAL TRANSCRIPTION, all deliberate: (1) framing item_text is the stimulus HTML rendered to plain text, so the source's paragraph breaks are lost and its leading 'Problem' heading survives as a word. (2) decision-rules item_text concatenates the source's problem_description and question fields, which are separate strings in the js but were shown together. (3) The per-item table of TV ratings is NOT reproduced: it is a 5x4 numeric matrix (table_numbers) rather than text, and it differs per item, so each dr item_text states the shopper's rule and the question but not the ratings a respondent was choosing between. (4) The decision-rules section_prompt is the second instruction page verbatim, followed by the rating legend quoted verbatim from the preceding practice page and marked as such, because the items refer to labels like 'Medium' and 'Very High' and are uninterpretable without it; the practice page's example table and three worked examples are not reproduced. option_text is populated only at the endpoints for framing items (label_min at resp 1, label_max at resp 6) because the source labels only the endpoints of the 6-point scale, and is blank throughout for decision-rules items because resp there is a count of correct options rather than a choice among them. correct_response carries the decision-rules answer letters, semicolon-separated where several are correct (dr8 'A;C', dr9 'A;D;E', dr10 'C;D;E'), and is blank for the framing items, which have no correct answer. NOT IN THIS TABLE: the ADMC risk-perception subtest. Its rows in the source store a stringified list of ten ids in a single admc_id cell ('[\'rp_a1\', ...]') rather than one row per item, so no rp_* code reaches IRW and the table holds 28 + 10 = 38 items. Recorded in case a future round wants those 20 items. AUDIT WARN EXPLAINED: audit_batch.R reports '71% of rows have blank option_text' and '10 of 38 items have NO option_text rows while others do (dr1, dr10, dr2, ...)'. Both describe the intended shape. The 10 decision-rules items carry no option_text at all because their resp is a count of correct options checked rather than a choice among labelled options, and the 28 framing items label only the two endpoints of their 6-point scale, as the source does; 25 dr rows plus the 112 unlabelled middle rows of the framing items give the 71%. An earlier run of this gate returned ERROR for this table on a Redivis timeout ('Less than 1 bytes/sec transferred the last 600 seconds'), which is transient and cleared on retry -- not a data condition.
public_note: Two ADMC subtests share this table and they are not on the same scale: the 28 Resistance to Framing items (codes a1_*, a2_*, rc1_*, rc2_*) use a 1-6 judgment scale whose endpoints only are labelled, while the 10 Applying Decision Rules items (dr1-dr10) are scored 0-3 as the NUMBER of correct options the respondent checked, not as a choice among options -- so resp is not comparable across the two blocks, and each dr item's maximum differs with how many answers it has (1 for dr1-dr7, 2 for dr8, 3 for dr9 and dr10). The decision-rules items also present a table of TV ratings that is a numeric matrix rather than text and is not reproduced here, so those item texts give the shopper's decision rule and the question but not the options being chosen between.
